title: Sec. 21-22(b)(56). - Updated exterior lighting policy.
sourceName: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Resolution No. 2024-05-04

text: Resolution No. 2024-05-04, adopted May 17, 2024, amends and replaces Sec. 21-22(b)(56), Lighting, effective immediately. DRC approval is required to modify or add exterior lighting, including motion detector spotlights, security lighting, landscape lighting, architectural accent lighting, decorative lighting, ballasted fixtures, and additional lighting at doors or windows. Cut sheets must be submitted to the Design Review Committee for each type of fixture proposed. All exterior lighting must comply with the Rules and Douglas County Dark Skies guidelines. Exterior lighting must be fully shielded, directed downward, warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less, and may be re-evaluated if it creates nuisance or complaints. Under-eave lighting provides architectural accent lighting. Canned lighting installed into front porch soffits or ceilings is included. Under-eave lighting must consist of hardwired fixtures installed into the soffit or hardwired track eave/rake lighting systems such as Jellyfish or Gemstone. Gemstone and Jellyfish systems are the approved systems. Other similar companies or products are not permitted unless added to the approved list of dark sky-compliant lighting systems. Under-eave lighting may be installed on the front of the home using logical termination points from the front to the sides; elevations showing termination points must be submitted with the application; termination points may not extend further than the wing fence. Under-eave lighting may be installed on the rear of the home if it backs up to open space, subject to DRC approval and case-by-case review. Corner lots can install under-eave lighting on the side of the home that abuts the street, subject to DRC approval and case-by-case review. Under-eave lighting shall not be used as security lighting. Hardwired canned lighting installed into the soffit or ceiling of the front porch shall light only the front porch and not extend beyond that area. Under-eave hardwired track eave/rake lighting systems or hardwired canned lighting can be installed under a roofed cover above a rear deck or rear patio, subject to DRC approval and case-by-case review, if the light cone does not cause glare to adjacent properties or onto the street and the light is warm, with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less. During non-holiday lighting periods, under-eave lighting must be warm white, static, and must not strobe, flash, pulse, chase, or use patterns outside approved architectural accent lighting. A homeowner may install traditional under-eave lighting, or use track lighting systems in a static pattern to accent the home architecturally. All under-eave lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. Decorative lighting must consist of cafe, globe, or lit rope style lights; LED string lights, holiday-decoration-style string lights, and other forms of lighting are not allowed as decorative lighting. Rear decorative lighting does not require DRC approval if located under a roofed cover above a rear deck or patio, if the light cone does not cause glare, and if it is warm white with a color temperature of 3,000 Kelvin or less. Landscape lighting must be low-level, downward-facing, warm white, and no taller than 36 inches for permitted solar in-ground lighting; no more than eight such fixtures are permitted in the front yard. Seasonal decorative lighting may include hardwired traditional soffit installed lighting, hardwired track eave/rake lighting, or temporary string lighting installed for the approved seasonal period. Seasonal decorative lighting should not create light trespass beyond property boundaries or glare onto surrounding properties. Temporary string lighting should use low-wattage lights; LED preferred. Seasonal decorative lighting may use colors and patterns and may blink, flash, chase, or strobe. Install and energize seasonal decorative lighting during the following approved seasonal lighting periods: from June 18 to July 7 and from October 1 through January 31. Outside those periods, temporary string lighting and clips must be removed, and hardwired traditional soffit installed lighting and hardwired track eave/rake lighting must be returned to the settings allowed in the under-eave lighting section. The CAB may extend removal dates due to extreme weather or other factors, but lighting may not be energized during that time. All holiday lighting must be turned off by 10:00 p.m. Security lighting must be directed at the ground and house, must stay within property boundaries, must not cause glare to other properties, cannot be on 24/7 except for the front of the home facing the public street, and must be photocell-controlled and motion-activated so it cannot stay on longer than five minutes once activated. Security lighting may be installed on the rear of the home if it backs up to open space, but is not permitted in the rear if the open space is a designated wildlife corridor.

text: Resolution No. 2024-11-02, adopted November 22, 2024, amends the CAB Code effective immediately. Section 21-22(b)(101), Trash Containers: Trash shall not be stored or allowed to accumulate on any property except within appropriate containers, which shall be properly stored in an enclosed structure, the garage, or appropriately screened from view behind the wing fence. Section 21-22(b)(63), Outdoor Decorative Objects: Rear yard DRC approval is not required for yard or lawn ornamentation in the rear yard when ornamentation does not exceed three feet in height; DRC approval is required over three feet. Front yard DRC approval is not required for yard or lawn ornamentation only when there are no more than three ornaments, items are placed on the ground, items do not exceed 12 inches in height or width, and items are integrated into the landscape design; DRC approval is required for front-yard ornaments that do not meet those provisions. Section 1-34(b), Signs; Flags: An Owner may display flags or political signage, subject to restrictions. No flag shall be prohibited or regulated on the basis of subject matter, message, or content, except that flags bearing commercial messages are prohibited. No flag shall exceed four feet by six feet. Section 21-22(b)(37) and (38), Flags and flag holders/flagpoles: The only flags allowed to be displayed on the front of the home are the United States flag, the Colorado flag, and certain permitted military service flags. Bracket flag holders on the home do not require DRC approval if the size is commensurate with the permitted flag. DRC approval is required for freestanding flagpoles and separate nighttime illumination of a flag.

sourceName: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Resolution 2024-11-03

text: Resolution 2024-11-03, Policy Governing Due Process and Imposition of Fines, adopted November 22, 2024. A proceeding may be initiated by complaint to or by the Community Standards Committee, or by CAB staff inspection. A warning letter advises the respondent of the complaint, the believed violation, and action needed within a specified time. If a violation is not cured not later than ten days after the warning letter or another stated date, or if a repetitious violation recurs within six months, CAB sends a Notice of Violation. The Notice of Violation must include the details, cure action, possible fines, the right to be heard orally or in writing by the Community Standards Committee at least fifteen days after notice, and the process to request a hearing. Continuous or repetitious violations fine schedule: Warning Letter $0.00; First Notice of Violation, 30 days to correct, $100.00; Second Notice of Violation, 14 days to correct, $250.00; Third Notice of Violation, 14 days to correct, $500.00; Continuing Violation $10.00 per day until cured. Nuisance violations fine schedule: Warning Letter $0.00; First Notice of Violation, 30 days to correct, $25.00; Second Notice of Violation, 14 days to correct, $50.00; Third Notice of Violation, 14 days to correct, $100.00; Continuing Violation $10.00 per day until cured. Owners are responsible for actions of tenants and guests. Fines may become a lien, but CAB shall not foreclose on a lien that arises from amounts owed as a result of a covenant violation or failure to comply with a Document.

sourceName: Sterling Ranch Community Authority Board Resolution No. 2025-06-01

text: Resolution No. 2025-06-01 establishes an amended and restated collection process for delinquent utility, monthly, and covenant enforcement fees and supersedes prior collection policies. Fees are delinquent when unpaid by their due date. Courtesy past due notification: three days after invoice due date by text, email, or automated phone call. Delinquent Account Late Fee: if not paid within seven calendar days after due date, a late fee is charged. Late Notice Letter: if unpaid on the 15th calendar day after due date, Provider sends a Late Notice Letter and charges a Late Notice Letter Fee. Disconnect Notice or Lien Notice: if unpaid on the 10th day of the month following invoice due date, Provider sends a Disconnect Notice Letter for delinquent Utility Fees or a Lien Notice Letter for delinquent Monthly Fees, by certified mail, and charges the applicable fee. Utility disconnect notice says failure to pay by the last Wednesday of the month will result in CAB disconnecting water service that day and describes hearing rights under Sections 29-41 or 29-42. Lien notice says failure to pay Monthly Fees by the last Wednesday of the month will result in CAB filing a notice of lien. Payment plans may be authorized for up to six months if the delinquent amount does not exceed $2,500; the General Manager may authorize longer terms or larger amounts. Exhibit A fees: Delinquent Account Late Fee 10% of delinquent amount not to exceed $15.00; Late Notice Letter Fee $5.00; Disconnect Notice/Lien Notice $25.00; 48 Hour Shut Off Notice Fee $50.00; Disconnect Fee $150.00; Reconnect Fee 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. $150.00; Reconnect Fee 3:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. $500.00; 9:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m. unavailable; Statement of Lien Filing Fee $250.00; Release of Statement of Lien Fee $100.00; Payment Plan Administration Fee $45.00 plus $10.00 per month; Returned Deposit Fee $20.00.
